heading: Free Online File Compressor for Images, Videos, Audio and Documents
introduction:
Managing large files can become difficult when you need to upload documents, share photos, send videos or store important data. Large files take longer to transfer, use more storage space and may not meet the size requirements of websites or online forms. A reliable file compression tool can help reduce these problems by making files smaller and easier to manage.

File Compresser provides free online tools for compressing and converting different types of files. You can work with images, videos, audio files, GIFs, PDFs and ZIP archives directly in your web browser. There is no need to install desktop software, create an account or upload your files to an external server. The processing takes place on your own device, giving you more control over your selected files.

Whether you want to reduce the size of a photograph, prepare a video for sharing, convert WAV audio into MP3 or organize several files into a ZIP archive, File Compresser brings these tools together in one place.

sections.heading: Compress Different File Types in One Place
sections.body: Different files need different compression methods. A photograph, PDF document and video recording cannot always be optimized using the same settings. File Compresser provides dedicated tools for common file formats so you can select the right option for your task.

sections.heading: Image Compression
sections.body:
Large images can slow down websites and create problems when uploading photographs or sharing design files. The image compression tools help reduce the size of supported JPG, JPEG, PNG and WebP images.

You can select an appropriate quality mode and compare the original image with the processed version. Image dimensions remain unchanged, so the compression result is easy to compare with the source.

The platform also provides separate tools for JPG, JPEG, PNG and WebP files. This makes it easier to choose settings according to the image format and its intended use.

sections.heading: Video Compression
sections.body:
Video recordings can take up considerable storage space, especially when they are long or recorded at high resolutions. The Video Compressor accepts supported MP4 and MOV files and converts them into MP4 using H.264 video encoding.

You can choose suitable output settings, including a resolution limit, according to your needs. Always check the final video before sharing it because the output size and visual quality depend on the original recording and selected settings.

sections.heading: Audio Compression and Conversion
sections.body:
Audio files also need different formats depending on where you plan to use them. The MP3 Compressor lets you re-encode existing MP3 files using a lower bitrate. This can reduce file size, although a lower bitrate may affect sound quality.

The WAV to MP3 Converter provides another option for people working with uncompressed audio recordings. Converting WAV files to MP3 can make them easier to store and share.

sections.heading: PDF Compression
sections.body:
PDF documents are commonly used for reports, forms, educational material and business records. Some PDF files can be difficult to email or upload because of their size.

The PDF Compressor attempts to optimize the document structure and selected metadata. However, it does not promise to reduce every PDF. Scanned documents and PDFs containing large images may remain close to their original size.

sections.heading: ZIP File Tools
sections.body: ZIP archives are useful when you need to collect multiple files into one package. The ZIP Creator helps combine selected files into a single archive, while the ZIP Extractor allows you to open supported ZIP files and save their contents. These tools are helpful for organizing documents, images and other files before sharing or storing them.

sections.heading: How Does File Compresser Work?
sections.body:
Using an online file compressor should not require technical knowledge. The process is designed around three simple steps.

Select your files: Open the tool you need and choose files from your device. You can also use the general compression page to process a supported mixed batch.
Choose your settings: Review the available compression or conversion options. Select settings according to the format and quality you need.
Review and download: Start processing and compare the original and final file sizes. Check the result before downloading it to your device.

The website also checks supported file types and size limits before processing. This helps identify files that cannot be handled by the selected tool.

sections.heading: Your Files Stay on Your Device
sections.body:
File Compresser processes selected files inside your browser. The files are read into the browser tab, processed using the required tools and made available for download. They are not sent to File Compresser servers for compression.

Because the work takes place in your browser, your device's memory and processing power can affect performance. Keep an original copy of important files before starting any compression task.

sections.heading: Why Use an Online File Compression Tool?
sections.body:
A useful file compressor should make everyday file tasks easier without hiding important details. File Compresser offers several practical benefits:

Free access: Use the available tools without creating an account or paying a subscription.
No installation: Open the website in a supported browser instead of installing separate compression software.
Private processing: Selected files are processed on your own device rather than uploaded to the website's servers.
Multiple formats: Work with supported images, videos, audio files, PDFs and ZIP archives.
No watermarks: Download processed files without an added File Compresser watermark.
Actual size comparison: Review the original and output sizes to understand whether compression made a difference.
Dedicated tools: Choose a format-specific tool when you need more control over the result.

sections.heading: When Should You Compress a File?
sections.body:
File compression is useful in many everyday situations. Website owners can optimize photographs before adding them to web pages. Students can prepare documents for online submissions. Professionals can reduce the size of email attachments, while content creators can prepare images, audio and videos for sharing.

The right settings depend on the purpose of the file. A website photograph may need a smaller file size, while a product image may require more visual detail. A voice recording may work well at a lower audio bitrate, but an important music or production file may need higher quality.

Always consider the final use before selecting compression settings.

sections.heading: Does Compression Always Make Files Smaller?
sections.body:
No. The result depends on the original file, its format and the selected settings. Some images are already optimized, while certain PDFs contain data that cannot be reduced through structural optimization alone.

File Compresser reports the actual result instead of promising a fixed percentage reduction. When ordinary same-format compression does not produce a smaller file, the original can be retained unchanged. Explicit conversions and ZIP creation may also increase the final file size.

For this reason, compare the actual output size and check the file quality before replacing your original.

sections.heading: Start Compressing Your Files Online
sections.body:
You do not need several applications for common file compression and conversion tasks. File Compresser brings image, video, audio, PDF and ZIP tools together in one accessible platform.

Choose the tool that matches your file and compare the result before downloading. See the Privacy Policy at https://File Compresser.com/privacy for how files are handled.

faq.q: Is File Compresser free to use?
faq.a: Yes. The available compression and conversion tools can be used without creating an account or paying a subscription.

faq.q: Do I need to install any software?
faq.a: No. You can open File Compresser in your web browser, select a tool and process supported files directly on your device.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded to File Compresser?
faq.a: No. Selected files are processed in your browser. The website downloads the required processing code, but your files are not uploaded to its servers.
Supported formats include JPG, JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP4, MOV, MP3, WAV, PDF and ZIP. Each tool has its own supported formats and file limits.

faq.q: Will compression reduce image or video quality?
faq.a: It depends on the selected settings. Lossy compression can change image or audio quality, and video re-encoding can affect visual detail. Review the result before downloading or using it.

faq.q: Why is my compressed file not smaller?
faq.a: Your original file may already be efficiently compressed. The tool may retain the original if a new version does not provide a smaller result.
